affiliations.role_title: Associate Professor of Psychology and Psychiatry; Director of Graduate Studies in Psychology
affiliations.research_notes: The institutional biography explicitly says Adams undertook 1943-1945 OSS assessment research while on military leave from Duke. The end year marks the transition into that leave, not a claim that his formal Duke appointment terminated.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Donald K. Adams is strongly matched to psychologist Donald Keith Adams, who conducted assessment research for OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The NARA index supplies the exact first name, surname, and middle initial; the institutional biography expands the middle name and explicitly documents 1943-1945 OSS assessment work.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name pattern plus an explicit OSS role supports a high-confidence match; Box 3 is not printed in the external biography, so the match is not labeled confirmed.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography dates the OSS assessment work to 1943-1945.
claims.match_notes: The 1943 Black Mountain College catalogue independently places Donald K. Adams at Duke in the transition year.

claims.claim_text: Donald Keith Adams's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was his psychology faculty employment at Duke University.
claims.evidence_excerpt: On military leave from Duke, Adams spent 1943–45 ... in assessment research for the Office of Strategic Services.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The institutional biography explicitly describes Adams's OSS work as military leave from Duke; the December 1943 college catalogue identifies his contemporary Duke psychology title.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact indexed name and middle initial align with the full-name biography, which explicitly documents OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The phrase military leave from Duke makes the Duke appointment the immediate civilian affiliation from which the OSS work began.
claims.match_notes: The historical role title follows the contemporary 1943 catalogue. The modeled 1943 endpoint marks entry into leave, not necessarily termination of the university appointment.

claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact indexed name and explicit OSS service support the person match; the contemporary catalogue corroborates the same middle-initialed Duke psychologist.
claims.temporal_assessment: The military-leave wording and 1943 catalogue jointly support Duke as the last documented civilian employer immediately before OSS work.
claims.match_notes: No claim is made that Adams's formal Duke employment ended during leave or that no undocumented short interval occurred.
